topics.title: DNS name resolution
topics.description: Explain, observe, diagnose and repair how a host turns a name into an address: the application calls the C library resolver, which consults `/etc/hosts`, reads `/etc/resolv.conf` and sends DNS queries over UDP/TCP port 53 to the configured nameservers, which answer from their zones or by recursion. Mastery means locating the failing hop with evidence (configuration, live queries, packets, listening sockets) and fixing the cause, not the symptom.

topics.title: How an application looks up a name
topics.description: Applications do not speak DNS. They call `getaddrinfo()`, which checks `/etc/hosts` first and only then asks DNS through the stub resolver. Tools like `dig` skip the first step, so they can disagree with what an application sees.

topics.title: Stub resolver and /etc/resolv.conf
topics.description: The stub resolver is the part of the C library that turns a name into DNS queries. It does not know any answers itself: it sends each query to the nameservers listed in `/etc/resolv.conf` and returns what they say.

topics.title: Reading a DNS answer
topics.description: A DNS reply carries a status code and records. `NOERROR` with an `A` record is an address; `NXDOMAIN` means the server answered that the name does not exist; no reply at all means the server was never reached. These point to different hops.
